steps: Convert any bfloat input contribution to float32 and form one float32 per-thread accumulator value.
Reduce each accumulator with simd_sum over the active threads of its SIMDgroup.
Have SIMDgroup lane zero write exactly one float32 partial per accumulator to that SIMDgroup's threadgroup-memory slot.
Execute threadgroup_barrier(mem_threadgroup) uniformly across all live threads after partial publication.
Have the selected final reducer load written partials and float32 zero for lanes beyond the live SIMDgroup count, then apply simd_sum.
If a final scalar is published for other SIMDgroups, have one owner lane store it and execute a second uniform threadgroup barrier before any cross-SIMDgroup consumer reads it.

scratch_lifecycle.initialization: Every scratch slot that can be read must either receive its lane-zero partial before the publication barrier or be initialized to float32 zero before that barrier.
scratch_lifecycle.initialization_barrier: When initialization is performed by threads other than the subsequent writer or reader, complete it with a uniform threadgroup_barrier(mem_threadgroup) before partial stores begin.
scratch_lifecycle.reuse_rule: Do not reuse partial or final-scalar scratch until all prior readers have crossed a uniform threadgroup_barrier(mem_threadgroup) separating the last read from the next write.
scratch_lifecycle.final_scalar_visibility_rule: A final scalar consumed outside its producing SIMDgroup must be published by an explicit owner and followed by a uniform threadgroup_barrier(mem_threadgroup) before consumption.

rms_norm.ownership: Only SIMDgroup zero performs the final reduction; one explicit lane-zero owner computes and publishes the scalar normalization factor.
rms_norm.publication: The owner stores one float32 final scalar in threadgroup memory.
rms_norm.consumer_barrier: Required when any other SIMDgroup consumes the published scalar.

layer_norm.ownership: Every SIMDgroup may load the same valid partial set and independently perform the same final simd_sum for each accumulator.
layer_norm.publication: No shared final scalar is required when each SIMDgroup retains its reduced float32 values in thread-local state.
layer_norm.consumer_barrier: Not required after the final reduction unless a later variant publishes shared output through reusable threadgroup scratch.

decisions.statement: Preserve the extracted candidate as width-neutral; do not promote the locally observed width of 32 into the candidate contract.
decisions.rationale: Apple explicitly forbids assuming SIMDgroup size, while the local observation covers only two pipelines on one M4 device.
alternatives: Make width 32 a family-wide candidate invariant.
Leave width behavior implicit in lowering.

decisions.statement: Refine one Apple-family specialization around width 32, selectable only after querying the selected pipeline and failing closed before dispatch on mismatch.
decisions.rationale: The guard preserves the hardware-neutral abstraction while enabling exact 1024/32 capacity arithmetic for the first locally observed specialization.
alternatives: Generate a width-polymorphic final reduction in the first implementation.
Silently fall back to another width or target when the query differs.

decisions.statement: Refine the candidate to simd_sum, lane-zero FP32 partial publication, a uniform threadgroup_barrier(mem_threadgroup), and a final simd_sum over valid partials and zero-filled unused lanes.
decisions.rationale: These Metal primitives directly realize the observed two-level source choreography while keeping publication and synchronization explicit.
alternatives: Use threadgroup memory for a full scalar reduction tree without simd_sum.
Use only SIMDgroup-local reduction and leave cross-SIMDgroup aggregation to another kernel.

decisions.statement: Split final-reducer ownership into RMS-style single-SIMDgroup publication and Layer-style all-SIMDgroup recomputation variants.
decisions.rationale: The two extracted observations differ materially in ownership and publication; hiding that difference would make synchronization and scratch lifetime unanalyzable.
alternatives: Force every operator to publish one final scalar.
Let lowering infer final-reducer ownership from use sites.

decisions.statement: Refine the specialization with a 32-partial FP32 ceiling of 128 bytes per accumulator, one combined aligned dynamic region per current operator variant, and a variant-specific total static-plus-dynamic memory gate.
decisions.rationale: Explicit arithmetic and layout keep both accumulator partials and broadcast scratch in the legality decision. RMS currently supplies one accumulator and one 4-byte scalar (132 raw, 144 aligned); Layer currently supplies two accumulators and no scalar (256 raw and aligned). These counts are variant inputs, not invariants of the generic candidate.
alternatives: Model only the partial array and omit the broadcast scalar.
Treat the family memory ceiling as sufficient without inspecting pipeline static allocation.

assumptions: The Stage-2 reviewer attestations correctly summarize the two bound source spans; this stage does not re-fetch or reinterpret their upstream code.
The cited vendor language revision and family tables are applicable to the later toolchain selected for human review.
The proposed mapping is confined to one Metal threadgroup; no cross-threadgroup communication is implied.

hypotheses.statement: The fail-closed width-32 specialization is available on the intended Apple-device and pipeline matrix often enough to be a useful retained specialization.

falsifier.method: Compile the future reduction pipeline on every intended device class and record threadExecutionWidth before dispatch.
falsifier.observable: Per-device and per-pipeline threadExecutionWidth plus whether guarded selection accepted or refused the specialization.
falsifier.reject_when: The intended deployment set materially requires a non-32 width and no separately reviewed specialization covers it.
falsifier.retained_result_contract: Append-only device-class and pipeline observation records that exclude stable device identifiers and preserve every refusal.

hypotheses.statement: A later analyzable compiler design can express exactly one FP32 partial per live SIMDgroup and accumulator together with explicit owner, initialization, barrier, and reuse effects.

falsifier.method: Run the P1-P8 principle review over a complete proposed primitive, typing rule, effects, verifier rules, analyses, and corpus cases.
falsifier.observable: Whether ownership, scratch lifetime, barrier participation, and one-partial cardinality are statically represented without hidden lowering inference.
falsifier.reject_when: The design requires implicit layout or ownership inference, unmodeled effects, or syntax whose analyses are deferred.
falsifier.retained_result_contract: A human-authored principle-review decision retaining each accepted and refused primitive shape with localized reasons.

hypotheses.statement: Representative future pipelines leave enough threadgroup memory and thread capacity for each variant's aligned combined allocation and all compiler-created static allocation.

falsifier.method: Compile every retained variant and inspect pipeline.staticThreadgroupMemoryLength, that variant's aligned dynamic allocation, device.maxThreadgroupMemoryLength, and maxTotalThreadsPerThreadgroup.
falsifier.observable: Total static-plus-dynamic bytes, alignment padding, requested threads, and both runtime ceilings for each pipeline variant.
falsifier.reject_when: Any retained configuration exceeds either runtime limit or the 32768-byte family ceiling.
falsifier.retained_result_contract: Append-only per-variant resource observations including refused configurations; no regenerated expectation may erase an overflow.

hypotheses.statement: The hierarchical FP32 reduction and its unspecified bitwise association satisfy the later Workload Contract's explicit numerical tolerances across required shapes and input distributions.

falsifier.method: Compare compiled end-to-end framework outputs with the external oracle across contract shapes, boundaries, tails, and adversarial input distributions.
falsifier.observable: Per-case absolute and relative error, non-finite behavior, and localized mismatch diagnostics.
falsifier.reject_when: Any required case violates its Workload Contract tolerance or demands bitwise-identical association.
falsifier.retained_result_contract: Append-only correctness-assay records bound to the Workload Contract, compiler revision, pipeline artifact, inputs, oracle, and all failed cases.

hypotheses.statement: At least one reviewed threadgroup size and per-thread work variant is performance-competitive for each intended workload shape without invalid resource pressure.

falsifier.method: After correctness, benchmark structurally distinct retained variants and collect profiler evidence under a fixed Workload Contract.
falsifier.observable: Latency distribution, throughput, occupancy or residency limits, register pressure, memory traffic, and diagnosed stalls relative to declared baselines.
falsifier.reject_when: No correct retained variant meets the predeclared performance criterion or profiling shows the mapping's resource structure is the limiting cause.
falsifier.retained_result_contract: Append-only correctness, timing, and profiler artifacts for every measured survivor, including negative and inconclusive outcomes.

falsifiers.condition: The selected MTLComputePipelineState reports threadExecutionWidth other than 32.
falsifiers.required_action: Reject this width-32 specialization before dispatch; do not rewrite the width-neutral candidate or silently fall back.

falsifiers.condition: Requested threads per threadgroup exceed the selected pipeline's maxTotalThreadsPerThreadgroup or the 1024 family ceiling.
threads_per_threadgroup is not an exact multiple of the queried runtime width.
falsifiers.required_action: Reject this v1 specialization; partial final SIMDgroups require a separately reviewed design even though Metal defines active-thread SIMDgroup semantics.

falsifiers.condition: ceil(threads_per_threadgroup/runtime_width) exceeds runtime_width, so one final SIMDgroup cannot hold all partials.
falsifiers.required_action: Reject this one-pass final-reduction design and return to hardware design for another hierarchy.

falsifiers.condition: Pipeline static threadgroup memory plus the selected variant's aligned combined dynamic region exceeds device.maxThreadgroupMemoryLength or the 32768-byte family ceiling.
falsifiers.required_action: Reject the design for that configuration rather than omit unmodeled memory.

falsifiers.condition: Any live thread can take an early return or divergent path around a required threadgroup barrier.
falsifiers.required_action: Reject the schedule or lowering as unsafe.

falsifiers.condition: A final reducer can read an unwritten partial or cross-SIMDgroup publication occurs without threadgroup_barrier(mem_threadgroup).
falsifiers.required_action: Reject the mapping as a data-consistency violation.

falsifiers.condition: Partial or final-scalar scratch can be overwritten before all prior readers cross the required reuse barrier.
falsifiers.required_action: Reject the lifetime plan or allocate distinct scratch.

falsifiers.condition: A lowering supplies bfloat directly to simd_sum instead of converting the contribution to float32.
falsifiers.required_action: Reject the lowering as outside the documented reduction-input contract.

falsifiers.condition: The RMS-style single owner versus Layer-style all-SIMDgroup final-reduction policy is absent or inferred implicitly.
falsifiers.required_action: Reject the design instance until ownership and publication are explicit.

falsifiers.condition: The eventual Workload Contract requires bitwise-identical reduction association or order.
falsifiers.required_action: Reject this mapping for that workload unless a separately reviewed deterministic numeric design satisfies the requirement.

falsifiers.condition: The implementation attempt still uses the current finite Metal lowering, which cannot allocate threadgroup scratch or emit the required barrier.
falsifiers.required_action: Stop before implementation; principle review and compiler-evolution design are required first.

open_questions: Which threadgroup size and per-thread work portfolio is performant across the intended M-series devices?
What register pressure and occupancy result from one versus multiple float32 accumulators?
Should a later general form admit partial final SIMDgroups, or preserve the whole-SIMDgroup restriction as a canonical legality rule?
Which explicit IR effects and verifier rules would represent threadgroup allocation, publication barriers, ownership, initialization, and reuse without introducing a layout algebra?

checks: Candidate and evidence bindings, exact resource formulas, width guard, barrier requirements, falsifier presence, and review-boundary fields are structurally consistent.
Validation does not decide that the mapping is safe, useful, canonical, correct, or performant.

blocking_reviews: Confirm vendor-fact interpretation, runtime width handling, resource accounting, barrier participation, scratch lifetime, and numeric scope.
Keep implementation unauthorized until the subsequent P1-P8 principle-driven iteration accepts an analyzable compiler-evolution design.

non_claims: This proposal is not an IR admission, Target mutation, lowering implementation, or assertion of current Schedule expressibility.
This proposal does not establish Metal correctness, race freedom, numerical tolerance, performance, occupancy, calibration, Evaluation evidence, or scientific results.
The 1024-thread and 32768-byte family limits are ceilings, not a launch authorization; the concrete pipeline and total allocation remain runtime and implementation gates.
Passing offline validation cannot set readiness=true or replace human hardware and principle review.
